notes: Handwritten example on affine groups: split sequence, diagonal section and translation inclusion, conjugation identity, equivariance criterion, and semidirect-product expressions.
The bracketed middle block discusses maps of sets with varying acting groups and uniqueness of the group homomorphism when the target is a torsor and the source is nonempty.
The lower blocks apply the construction to a vector space and to affine transformations preserving the quadratic distance.

The page has an underlined Ex and two underlined NB forms, the first canceled. There is no date or manuscript page number; archive foliation 9 is a comment. No cotefile macro is repeated on scan 10, following the supplied brief.
No authorial question or doubt word is securely written. The superscript on tau has an unresolved cancellation state; the orange doubt macros are editorial.
The raised clause et E ≠ empty and grpe ss-jacent à are insertions with connectors; Q is interlinear. Ordinary manuscript wraps were joined, with the four main paragraphs retained.
Preserve the right-side block as vertically stacked and the lower membership signs. The long reference arrow remains on this page and points to its own heading.
The product annotation has a clear closing parenthesis; its opening remains uncertain. No opening delimiter was supplied merely to balance it.
The symbols around tau and the crossed group operators were read without importing a translation convention. Mathematical checks are confined to the two separately listed claims.
S.json is empty: there are no sweep rows to confirm or overturn.

Workflow: whole page once for layout, then half a once and half b once, then one enhanced crop per listed unresolved locus. All 18 crops were actually displayed. No OCR, recognition library, PDF text, external research, other page, other reader, or TeX compilation was used.

checks.statement: If E′ is a G′-torsor and E is nonempty, rho determines gamma in the displayed equivariance condition.
checks.reasoning: Choose x in E. If gamma_1 and gamma_2 both satisfy the condition, gamma_1(g).rho(x)=rho(g.x)=gamma_2(g).rho(x). Freeness of the G′ action implies gamma_1(g)=gamma_2(g) for every g.
checks.outcome: The written uniqueness claim is valid under its displayed hypotheses. The E′/G′ primes were independently read from the half.

checks.statement: The lower affine composition law is (z,gamma).(z′,gamma′)=(z+gamma(z′),gammagamma′).
checks.reasoning: For the affine action f_(z,gamma)(v)=z+gamma(v), composition gives z+gamma(z′+gamma′(v))=z+gamma(z′)+(gammagamma′)(v).
checks.outcome: The displayed law agrees with this action convention. This calculation was not used to determine any doubtful glyph.
